correctness.rationale: Checked the primary transfer matrix Tr(prod [[a_i,−ell²/2],[1,0]]) for open chamber 0<2ell<min a_i and the correct dimensional normalization. For each upper coordinate facet x_i=a_i, support motion ∂V/∂a_i contributes U_i+D_i/sqrt(2); ∂V/∂ell=−ΣD_i/sqrt(2). Divergence/normal equilibrium dotted with all-ones gives ΣU_i=ΣL_i (diagonal normals sum zero in that direction), so total ordinary Euclidean S=2Σ∂_{a_i}V+(2−sqrt(2))∂_ell V. Homogeneous uniform scaling A with fixed ell=t gives Σ∂_{a_i}V=sf_s−tf_s′, so S_s formula follows. Tr(M(t)^s) eigenvalues λ±=(1±sqrt(1−2t²))/2. Brunn–Minkowski makes h=f_s^{1/s} concave under affine interpolation; strictness follows because different t have distinct volumes but all coordinate widths are exactly 1, so two bodies cannot be positive homothets. The derivative Q′=s(2−sqrt(2)−2t)h″, h″≤0 and not identically zero on any interval, yields strict descent then ascent across t*=1−1/sqrt(2). At optimum the derivative term vanishes. Formula and continuity at t=0,1/2 are not illegitimate differentiation across chamber boundaries. Independently checked transfer matrix trace numerically in 25 sample (s,t) cases and symbolic derivative algebra; finite cases do not prove global uniqueness.
